plan.title: KittyCreditLine.deposit mints share units at pool price, with a two-LP test
plan.fix: deposit(): compute BEFORE the transfer `uint256 value = poolValue(); uint256 units = (totalDeposits == 0 || value == 0) ? amount : amount * totalDeposits / value; if (units == 0) revert ZeroAmount();` then `deposits[msg.sender] += units; totalDeposits += units; ASSET.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount); emit Deposited(msg.sender, amount);` (event keeps the kUSD amount so test_depositEmitsAndTracks line 264 still passes; no ABI change, so worker/abi/KittyCreditLine.json and web/src/abi/KittyCreditLine.json stay). Rounding down is the safe direction. NatSpec lines 23-24: 'fees repaid by borrowers stay in the pool and raise every LP's entitlement; `deposits` and `totalDeposits` are share units, not kUSD'. Tests: add `address lp2 = address(0x2);` next to `lp` (line 30) and two tests: (a) test_secondLpDoesNotCaptureEarlierFees: `_provenOnTime(AMOUNT, 1); _fundPool(100e6);` (limit is 20 kUSD, see line 222 comment); as alice `credit.borrow(20e6)`, then `usd.mint(alice, 1e6)`, approve and `credit.repay(21e6)`; `assertApproxEqAbs(credit.entitlement(lp), 101e6, 1)`; mint/approve/deposit 100e6 as lp2; `assertApproxEqAbs(credit.entitlement(lp), 101e6, 1); assertApproxEqAbs(credit.entitlement(lp2), 100e6, 1);` (b) test_fullExitAfterFees: same setup without lp2, lp calls `withdraw(credit.entitlement(lp))`, assert `deposits(lp)==0`, `totalDeposits==0`, `usd.balanceOf(lp)==101e6`. Run `forge test` (expect 102 passing; existing test_liquidityConstraints deposits before any fee so it hits the 1:1 branch unchanged). Hand the new count to item 9.
plan.why: README line 312 claims 'withdrawals are pro-rata over pool value' but deposit() is not the mirror of withdraw(): a late LP buys units at par and instantly captures accrued fees (reproduced: LP1 101.00 → 100.50 the moment LP2 joins). An engineer reading the 30-line LP section sees the asymmetry.

plan.title: Steward liveness: quarantine unknown-circle and wrong-amount payments instead of retrying a reverting batch forever
plan.fix: (a) Line 80: `let circle; try { circle = await ledger.getCircle(circleId); } catch (e) { const why = revertReason(e, ledger.interface); if (why.startsWith('UnknownCircle')) { for (const p of list) state.recorded[p.txHash] = true; pending.delete(key); log(`ignoring ${list.length} payment(s) to unknown circle ${circleId}`); continue; } throw e; }` (today the throw exits tick() before closeRounds/payouts and the entry pins lastSourceBlock at line 58, so one 1-unit deposit to circleId 999999 stops every circle until state is hand-edited; reproduced on local anvils). (b) Split the skip at lines 81-85: when `Number(circle.status) !== 0` (Completed) or `round < Number(circle.currentRound)` mark every tx in `list` `state.recorded[...] = true` before `pending.delete(key)` because the ledger can never accept them; keep the un-marked delete for `round > currentRound` and `circle.open`. (c) Insert BEFORE the `seen` check at line 95: `if (p.amount !== circle.contribution) { state.recorded[p.txHash] = true; log(`ignoring wrong-amount payment by ${p.member}: ${Number(p.amount) / 1e6} tUSD, installment is ${Number(circle.contribution) / 1e6} (${p.txHash.slice(0, 12)}…)`); continue; }` — it must precede the duplicate check, otherwise a member's corrected payment is marked as a 'duplicate' of the wrong one and lost (reproduced: WrongAmount(50000000, 100000000) every tick, correct tx persisted as recorded, all three members marked missed). `circle.contribution` is in the getCircle struct (KittyLedger.sol line 65). (d) In the catch at 137-140 add `record({ kind: 'error', summary: `batch failed: ${why}`, evidence: { ...decision.evidence, revert: why } })` so the decision log shows the failure. Never quarantine on any other error (RPC, ProofRejected). Verify: `pnpm typecheck`; then in a local world (`WORLD_ROUND1=0 scripts/local-world.sh`, env from item 6) run `cast send $KITTY_VAULT_ADDRESS 'contribute(uint256,uint32,uint256)' 999999 0 1 --rpc-url $SEPOLIA_RPC_URL --private-key <anvil key #4>` and `pnpm -s demo contribute`, then `pnpm -s worker --once` must log the two 'ignoring' lines and prove the round; `pnpm scenarios` and `pnpm e2e:local` still pass.
plan.why: Anyone on Sepolia can halt the live steward with one transaction to the public vault (no membership check, KittyVault.sol:62-68); the worker's own comment at lines 68-69 claims stray payments are handled. A Creditcoin engineer reading the 272-line loop finds both holes in minutes.

plan.title: Batch policy respects the Proof Builder's 1000-block window and reports only what the batch actually contains
plan.fix: (1) Add `export const MAX_BATCH_RANGE = 1000;` under MAX_BATCH with the comment 'the Proof Builder batch endpoint rejects spans of 1000+ blocks with BatchSpanTooLarge (verified against prover.cc3-testnet); leftovers go in a later call'. Replace line 97 `sorted.slice(0, MAX_BATCH)` with a greedy fill: `const batch: PendingPayment[] = []; for (const p of sorted) { if (batch.length >= MAX_BATCH) break; if (batch.length) { const lo = Math.min(p.block, ...batch.map((b) => b.block)); const hi = Math.max(p.block, ...batch.map((b) => b.block)); if (hi - lo >= MAX_BATCH_RANGE) continue; } batch.push(p); }`. (2) Lines 99-103: compute `inRound` from `batch` (not `best`) and count distinct members: `return new Set(inRound.map((p) => p.member.toLowerCase())).size >= inRound[0].circleSize;`. (3) evidence: add `blockSpan: Math.max(...batch.map((p) => p.block)) - Math.min(...batch.map((p) => p.block))` and `leftBehind: sorted.length - batch.length`. (4) Tests to add (fixtures per the existing `pay`/`frontier` helpers): 'never pools payments more than 1000 blocks apart' (one payment at block 100 plus nine at 1500-1508, all closeHeight 5000, frontier(2000,2000), force:true → every batch has max(block)-min(block) < 1000 and `evidence.leftBehind > 0`); 'a full batch only counts rounds it fully contains' (3 payments circle 1 size 3 closeHeight 5000 + 8 payments circle 2 size 8 closeHeight 4000, frontier(1500,1500) → reason 'full', `evidence.roundsCompleted === 1`); 'duplicate payments by one member do not complete a round' (three `pay({ member: '0xaa' })` in a size-3 circle → reason !== 'round-complete'); 'waited' (one payment seenAt 0, `{ waitMs: 45_000, now: 46_000 }` → reason 'waited', explainBatch matches /waited 46s/); 'forced' (force:true → 'forced'); 'equal slack: the larger group wins' (chainKey 3 with two payments vs chainKey 1 with one, same closeHeight → chainKey 3). `pnpm test:agent` → 26 passing; the existing 'fires immediately when a round is complete' test must still pass (all three fit one batch). Hand the new count to item 9 (README line 181 says 8).
plan.why: Reproduced: >10 ready payments make roundsCompleted count a round the batch only partly contains, and that number enters the citable decision log Layer 3 is allowed to quote — the 'agent that cannot lie' rests on the log being right. And a backlog after a restart pools payments 1000+ blocks apart, which the live Proof Builder rejects (BatchSpanTooLarge), silently degrading to N single calls while the log says 'in one call'.

summary: A judge who opens the repo will find a demo video that plays (with chapters), a deck, an integration write-up and a DoraHacks text that all describe the same v2 product as the README — eight scenarios, 100+ tests, per-circle chain keys, a deadline + 64 attested clock, a truthful ChainInfo count and an honest statement of which key holds the operator role — instead of a 404, a five-scenario deck and a '27 tests, pinned chain key' doc. The dashboard stops contradicting the pitch: the public /lab shows all eight scenarios with a recorded run, a new /steward page surfaces the decision log and the citation validator, the prove panel asks 0x0FD3 which attestation covers each payment and simulates the ledger before spending gas, and the score page never invents a 500. Under the hood the steward can no longer be halted by one stray Sepolia transaction, respects the Proof Builder's 1000-block batch window, logs only figures its batch actually earned, `pnpm judge` runs every advertised check on a fresh clone, and the credit line and final-round payout close two accounting holes an engineer would have found by reading the contracts.
